text: At the funeral. <break time="0.8s" /> Marcher stood among strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> Treated as no more than a distant acquaintance. <break time="0.8s" /> For he possessed no recognized right. <break time="0.8s" /> To grieve for a woman. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had been nothing to him in name. <break time="0.8s" /> Unable to bear the emptiness of London. <break time="0.8s" /> He travelled for a long time in the East. <break time="0.8s" /> But the wonders of Asia seemed dull to him. <break time="0.8s" /> Compared with the one small grave. <break time="0.8s" /> He had left behind. <break time="0.8s" /> On his return. <break time="0.8s" /> He went to her grave again and again. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he would sit for hours. <break time="0.8s" /> On the cold stone. <break time="0.8s" /> As if by staying near her. <break time="0.8s" /> He might recover some lost part of himself. <break time="0.8s" /> One autumn afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> At a fresh grave nearby. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw a mourner. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose face was so ravaged by grief. <break time="0.8s" /> That Marcher, as the man passed. <break time="0.8s" /> Felt as if he had been struck. <break time="0.8s" /> Never in his life. <break time="0.8s" /> Had Marcher felt a passion like that and he saw. <break time="0.8s" /> With a terrible clearness. <break time="0.8s" /> That the stranger had lived and loved. <break time="0.8s" /> Whereas he himself had merely waited. <break time="0.8s" /> The truth he had missed. <break time="0.8s" /> Now stood before him in all its horror. <break time="0.8s" /> Namely that he was the man of his time. <break time="0.8s" /> To whom nothing on earth was ever to happen. <break time="0.8s" /> The escape would have been to love her. <break time="0.8s" /> For then, and only then. <break time="0.8s" /> Would he have truly lived. <break time="0.8s" /> And May who had seen this long ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Had offered him that escape in vain. <break time="0.8s" /> At that moment. <break time="0.8s" /> He seemed to see the Beast at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Huge and hideous. <break time="0.8s" /> Rising for its long delayed leap. <break time="0.8s" /> And to avoid it. <break time="0.8s" /> He flung himself face down upon her tomb.
